stem: What is the key surgical principle of the Soave procedure for Hirschsprung disease?

options.text: Straight end-to-end anastomosis after full resection
Pull-through of normal colon through an aganglionic muscular cuff
Side-to-side anastomosis in the retrorectal plane

explanation: Pull-through of normal colon through an aganglionic muscular cuff is the defining principle of the Soave procedure, which preserves the rectal muscular cuff while bringing ganglionated bowel down through it.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this describes a resection with end-to-end anastomosis, which is not the Soave procedure.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the Soave procedure leaves an aganglionic muscular cuff of rectum in place and pulls normal ganglionated colon through it.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this describes the Duhamel procedure, not the Soave procedure.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because colectomy with ileostomy is not the defining operative principle of the Soave procedure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the Soave procedure is a pull-through operation, not simply a resection without reconstruction.

source.hint: Consider the technique that focuses on preserving the pelvic nerves by working within a 'cuff' of the rectum.
